title: Quantifying force-field and partial-charge uncertainty in high-throughput grand canonical Monte Carlo screening of metal–organic frameworks for CO 2  capture
content: Grand-canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) screens rank metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 capture, but their force field and partial-charge scheme are chosen by convention. Here one such family of screens is analysed as a measurement system: in a gauge repeatability and reproducibility (R&R) study of the CRAFTED database, its rigid MOFs are the parts and its 12 generic force-field and charge-scheme protocols the appraisers (pure CO2 and N2, 273–323 K, 0.1–10 bar). At flue-gas conditions (CO2, 298 K, 0.1 bar) the measurement system, nearly all of it the protocol, accounts for 32% of the variance in predicted uptake across 632 MOFs (% GRR 56%, AIAG study variation; 42–62% with protocols resampled), and the signal-to-noise ratio is 2.1 (1.8–3.1): about two classes of material. The dominant error is material-specific interaction, not a global bias; charges derived from or trained on DFT lower % GRR only to 33%. Only three of one protocol's top-10 MOFs survive in another's. Protocol sensitivity is partly predictable from structure (R2 = 0.43): narrow pores, light metals and polar linkers fare worst, and metal-free covalent organic frameworks no better. In 330 new RASPA3 runs, replicates scatter half as much as the database's reported uncertainty for the same MOFs: the low resolution is protocol disagreement, not noise. CRAFTED's shifted-potential cut-off gives uptakes 20% below tail-corrected ones, which do not depend on the cut-off distance. Ten of 21 published uptakes of rigid frameworks lie outside the whole protocol range, nine below it. Such screens should report % GRR and NDC with their rankings.
